reason: The dense knot and neighboring cold cloud seem like a direct way to investigate whether the surviving clumps can form stars.
expectation: The cold gas may join the knot and help it collapse, perhaps forming new stars.

alternatives.reason: The young stars may reveal what happens to dust in their light, but I want to follow the surviving clumps first.

effect: The surviving clumps helped form young stars, completing that goal; I will now follow the dust.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the old pillars' material become stars beyond the nursery.
reason: The young stars and nearby dusty gas can show what happens to dust exposed to their light.
expectation: The starlight may heat the dust and make it emit radiation, though I am unsure what the game will show.

alternatives.reason: The outflow could carry dust away, but I want to explore the starlight path first.

effect: The dust absorbs starlight and radiates in infrared; the dust goal remains open, so I will follow the outflow path.
reaction: The distinction between glowing gas and warmed dust is interesting.
reason: Combining the outflow with nearby dusty gas follows the other path described in the chapter.
expectation: The outflow may carry some dust away from the nursery, though I do not know where it will end up.

alternatives.reason: The warmed dust might also travel with the outflow, but I want to follow the separate dust portion first.

effect: The outflow carries dust outward, with some grains sheltered in clumps; the remaining action can follow it into the outer gas.
reaction: The difference between sheltered and exposed grains makes their journey more interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it follows the dust into the galaxy's hot outer gas.
expectation: The dust will encounter the hot outer gas, which may alter or destroy some exposed grains.

effect: The hot outer gas erodes many dust grains, completing the dust goal and the chapter.
reaction: The grains returning their material to the gas was a satisfying conclusion to their journey.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the surviving clumps into new stars was most worthwhile: it connected the old pillars to a new generation beyond the nursery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Carrying dust outward was less engaging on its own because it mainly set up the later encounter with hot gas.

surprise.text: I was interested that warmed dust radiates in infrared without forming another star, and that later exposure to hot gas can erode the grains.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly purposeless, though the final hotspot was the only offered move rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how the dispersed material and young stars evolve, though the offered combinations made the choices fairly guided.
